title: AetherAI - Redwood migration discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand AetherAI's current usage of OpenAI and options for migrating to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Key concerns: latency, cost, eval parity, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stack, and security (SOC 2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: share security pack, propose pilot plan, run small benchmark against their vLLM setup.
topics: Current stack: OpenAI + vLLM for on-prem inference
Production pain points: latency variability, cost spikes, KV cache and batching
Compatibility concerns: model parity across Redwood and vLLM/TGI runtimes
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
Security & compliance: SOC 2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Pilot scope and success criteria: latency, cost per token, eval-quality parity
next_steps: Redwood to send security questionnaire and SOC2 report (Lena) by 2026-08-03
SE to prepare benchmark plan and scripts to compare Redwood Dedicated vs their vLLM baseline (Marco) by 2026-08-07
Customer to share sample prompt set and eval metrics for parity checks (Priya) by 2026-08-04
Schedule technical deep-dive / bench run next week (30-60m) - tentative 2026-08-10
action_items: Lena Park: Send security pack + SOC2 + SSO docs (due 2026-08-03)
Marco Silva: Draft benchmark plan + resource reqs for Dedicated pilot (due 2026-08-07)
Priya Mehta: Provide representative prompt set + current eval reports (due 2026-08-04)
Tom Nguyen: Confirm compliance team availability for review (due 2026-08-05)
meeting_header: 2026-08-01 15:00 PDT | 45 minutes | Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Silva (Redwood) / Priya Mehta, Tom Nguyen, Sarah Lopez (AetherAI)
transcript: [00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick introductions — I'm Lena, AE on the Redwood team, and Marco here is our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Marco: Hi all, glad to be here. We'll try to understand your current infra and where Redwood might fit, especially around migrating from OpenAI and your vLLM setup.

[00:30] Priya: Thanks. Quick context: we run customer-facing summarization and routing. Currently using OpenAI for model access, and for on-prem fast paths we run vLLM/TGI on our infra. We're seeing cost and latency issues at scale.
[00:48] Tom: Yeah, cost unpredictability is a big pain; also needing consistent eval parity when switching models or runtimes, we can't degrade quality for customers.
[01:05] Marco: Understood. When you say vLLM/TGI, are you using TGI-based adapters or straight vLLM serving with KV cache optimized for decoder-only models?
[01:22] Priya: Mostly vLLM with some TGI experiments. We do heavy prefix caching for chat history — the KV cache is central to our latency SLA.
[01:40] Lena: Great, that matters a lot. On Redwood Dedicated we optimize KV cache handling and batching, and we can pin model versions. Curious about your QPS and p50/p95 latency goals?
[01:58] Sarah: Our production p50 is ~120ms token and p95 under 600ms at current load, but spikes hit 1.5s which is unacceptable. QPS average is about 60 concurrent request streams, peak 220.

[02:20] Marco: Okay. For Dedicated we can size GPU pools to hit those p95 targets; also we can route critical traffic to dedicated pools and fall back to hosted. Are you looking for Hosted or Dedicated or full Private/VPC?
[02:38] Tom: We're evaluating. Preferred is Dedicated for predictable throughput, but for regulated customers we may need Private/VPC. Question is migration complexity and whether eval parity holds.
[02:55] Priya: Exactly — our evaluators run datasets to confirm output quality. If we move from OpenAI/vLLM to Redwood runtime, we need near-identical outputs for our fine-tuned prompts.

[03:12] Marco: On model parity: Redwood supports the same open model families and can run standard FP16/quantized variants. Small differences can happen due to tokenization and kernel selection; we do evals with your prompt set to measure exact delta.
[03:30] Priya: Good to hear. Also wondering about compatibility with TGI configs — can Redwood accept your saved TGI checkpoints or do we need to recompile models?

[03:47] Marco: We support many checkpoints but sometimes require a model conversion step; it's usually automated. For TGI-specific patching, we can walk through a conversion; we should test with one model first.
[04:05] Tom: What about quantization — we rely on int8/4 to reduce cost. How well does Redwood preserve quality at those quant levels compared to our current setup?

[04:22] Marco: We have quantization profiles per model and workload. In general int8 is robust; int4 gains cost but can introduce small regressions. Part of the pilot is to run your evals across quant and non-quant configs.
[04:39] Lena: Also security — do you require SOC 2, SAML, KMS integration, or on-prem HSM?
[04:47] Priya: Yes SOC 2 is required, plus we use Okta SAML SSO and customer-managed KMS for encryption keys. For some customers we need on-prem options.
[05:05] Marco: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can be deployed in VPC or on-prem. We'll include the SOC 2 report and SSO integration guide in the security pack.
[05:20] Tom: Great. On the ops side, how do you handle fallbacks? If a dedicated pool runs out of capacity, can requests go to hosted or to a lower-cost model?
[05:32] Marco: Yes — smart routing policies let you fallback to a compatible variant or region. You can set latency and cost thresholds and the router will pick the best path.

[05:48] Priya: For benchmarks, we already run a baseline on vLLM: scripts that exercise prefix-heavy chat and a summarization job. We want to run the same script against Redwood Dedicated to compare p95 and cost/token.
[06:05] Marco: Perfect — please share the scripts. We'll run them in a dedicated pilot and provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces.

[06:20] Lena: Quick pricing question — what's the expected delta between running on OpenAI vs Redwood Hosted/Dedicated? We discussed unit economics previously but we'll tailor a proposal after seeing volumes.
[06:35] Tom: We need conservative estimates; procurement will require a comparison with committed Dedicated pricing vs pay-as-you-go.
[06:45] Marco: We'll include committed capacity quotes. For Dedicated customers we also provide burst options and SLA targets.
[07:00] Sarah: A couple of nuanced questions: does your runtime support custom kernels we use, and are there known differences in determinism for sampling seeds?

[07:15] Marco: We support custom kernel selection on some stacks; determinism can vary with GPU and kernel versions. If determinism is required we can run controlled experiments and document any nondeterministic sources.
[07:33] Priya: Another issue — we have audit requirements around PII. Do you offer data redaction or field-level logging controls?
[07:45] Marco: We support audit logs, token-level tracing, and can configure data retention windows. For PII redaction we can integrate pre-processing steps or work with your team on hooks.
[08:00] Tom: On the technical side, what is the expected work to onboard one of our internal models? We want to avoid long model conversion cycles.

[08:15] Marco: Typically we run a model onboarding checklist: model artifact transfer, basic validation, conversion (if needed), and one bench run. For many customers this is 2-4 business days for straightforward models.
[08:32] Lena: We'll propose a short pilot: 2-3 models, run your eval set, compare costs and latency. If that passes, we can scope a Dedicated commit and timeline for Private if needed.
[08:50] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Regarding monitoring, do you expose per-route traces so we can hook into our observability stack (Datadog, Prometheus)?
[09:02] Marco: Yes — Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, traces, and token-level breakdowns. We have integrations with common stacks and can provide the API for exports.
[09:18] Sarah: Any gotchas when switching tokenizers or merges? We've seen tokenization differences cause output shifts.
[09:30] Marco: Good point — tokenization can change outputs. We'll run tokenization parity checks as part of the evals and flag any drift.
[09:45] Priya: If we find minor quality deltas, what's the remediation path? Retrain or prompt engineering?
[09:55] Marco: Usually we try prompt tuning first, then quantization adjustments; retraining or fine-tuning is last resort. We'll include suggested mitigations in the bench report.
[10:12] Tom: From procurement perspective we'll need a paper trail: security docs, pricing, SLA. Lena, can you coordinate with our procurement contact?
[10:22] Lena: Absolutely — I'll send the security pack and a draft pilot agreement. We'll include pricing scenarios for Dedicated capacity and burst options.

[10:38] Priya: For the pilot success criteria: parity within X% on rouge/accuracy on our evals, p95 under 700ms, and cost reduction target of 15% compared to current OpenAI+vLLM hybrid. Are those realistic?
[10:55] Marco: Those are reasonable targets to test. We'll measure delta and propose config changes (quantization, batching) to hit cost/latency goals.
[11:10] Sarah: Also want to confirm SSO flow and provisioning for engineers during pilot, we use Okta and SCIM for user provisioning.
[11:22] Lena: We'll include SSO/SCIM docs and can provision sandbox access for your team.
[11:35] Tom: Any limits on model size or custom kernels for Dedicated vs Private?
[11:45] Marco: Dedicated can handle large models; Private/on-prem gives the most control for custom kernels. We'll share a checklist for model artifacts and expected GPU requirements.
[11:58] Priya: One random question — do you support function calling / structured outputs similarly to OpenAI? We rely on those for downstream parsing.
[12:10] Marco: Yes, we support streaming, function-like structured outputs and tool calling patterns. We'll demo that in a follow-up if helpful.
[12:25] Lena: Ok, let's recap: Redwood will send security pack + SOC2, Marco will draft benchmark plan, AetherAI will share prompt set/eval scripts, and we'll schedule bench run. Any other items?
[12:40] Priya: Nothing else from me. Thanks — excited to see results.
[12:46] Tom: Thanks everyone. We'll review internally once we get the docs.
[12:52] Lena: Thanks all, talk soon — we'll follow up with calendar invite for the bench run.
